clue.text: Lady occasionally entering shed for break from work

indicators.note: the picked letters go into the middle of the word for shed, as if walking into it

parts.note: to doff is to take off or shed clothing

indicators.note: taking only every other letter of the word Lady, the ones appearing now and then

explanation.surface: A woman nips out to the garden shed for a breather from her work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden hut but is the verb, to take off clothes; 'occasionally' picks the even letters of Lady and 'entering' puts them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest day when no work is done is a pause or break from one's job.

clue.text: Pass Europeans on vacation coming to order salad

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: emptied out, as a house is on holiday, leaving only the outer letters of Europeans

parts.note: law and order go together; law means order kept by rules

explanation.surface: Travellers crossing a mountain pass from Europe stop to order a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' empties Europeans to ES; 'coming to' just joins it to LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded cabbage dressed with mayonnaise is a familiar cold side salad.

clue.text: Criticise judge initially, and strange potentate

parts.note: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word judge is taken

parts.note: rum is old-fashioned British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A critic hauls a judge over the coals, and a peculiar ruler too.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompous self-important official or ruler is mockingly called by this grand title, a mock-important potentate.

clue.text: Act topping bill I learned trashed hotel previously

indicators.note: says the hotel letter comes earlier, before the rest

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: wrecked or messed up, so the letters of I learned are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock star confesses to having learned to trash a hotel room before the gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trashed' rearranges I LEARNED to EADLINER; 'previously' puts H in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The star performer whose name is printed biggest on a concert poster tops the bill.

clue.text: Reported dilemma for voters in capital city

indicators.note: signals that what is said out loud is heard as the entry

parts.note: a voter's dilemma is which candidate to support: 'back who?'

explanation.surface: A news report on voters torn over whom to support in a capital's election.
explanation.walkthrough: The dilemma is the question 'Back who?', which said out loud gives the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Caspian Sea is the capital of Azerbaijan.

clue.text: Spots King wearing glasses

indicators.note: the glasses go on around the king letter, as clothing is worn around a body

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: The monarch puts on his spectacles to spot something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb but is the noun, small marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny dots or flecks are small spots on a surface.

clue.text: Live male insect, enormous thing

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
he is the male pronoun
a moth is a winged insect

explanation.surface: A live male insect described as something gigantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant beast from the Book of Job, the word now names anything huge and monstrous.

clue.text: Current difficulty that involves very old tree

indicators.note: takes in, so the very old letters go inside the current letters

parts.note: AC is alternating current
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: An electrical fault involving a very old tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit with the big stone grows on a tropical evergreen of the laurel family.

clue.text: Steer around really discontented antelope

indicators.note: the ox goes round the other letters

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

indicators.note: contents removed, leaving only the outer letters of really

explanation.surface: A grumpy antelope being steered around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb but is the noun, a bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: A large straight-horned antelope of African and Arabian deserts.

clue.text: Former partner given more than enough warning?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
ample means plentiful, more than sufficient

explanation.surface: An ex-partner who has had plenty of warnings already.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the looser definition: someone punished to deter others is made an example of.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishment made public to deter others serves as a caution, a lesson to the rest.

clue.text: Delighted about little woman meeting Yankee journalist

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a row over money
Jo is one of the March sisters in Little Women
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at a small woman meeting an American reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling great joy is the same as being thrilled or delighted.

clue.text: Article stolen from dirty relative

indicators.note: taken away, so the article letters are removed from the word for dirty

parts.note: unclean means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item nicked from a grubby family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family relative.

clue.text: Recall number virtually abandoned convicted offender

indicators.note: call back, read in reverse, so the assembled letters run backwards
almost entirely, so the last letter of the word for abandoned is dropped

parts.note: left means abandoned

explanation.surface: A recalled number almost gets abandoned, like a convicted criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: NO plus LEF (left less its last letter) gives NOLEF, which 'Recall' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone found guilty of a serious crime.

clue.text: Painting technique chimp astonishingly possesses

indicators.note: holds within it, so the letters lie inside the words chimp astonishingly

explanation.surface: An ape turns out to be remarkably skilled at painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying paint on thickly so brush strokes stand proud is a recognised painting method.

clue.text: Pardon main criminal, temperamental type

indicators.note: wrong or lawless, so the letters of Pardon main are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to pardon the chief criminal, who is a moody sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun but is an adjective signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain, demanding diva-like person is a temperamental type, from the leading opera singer.

clue.text: Sport duke plays is game with many variations

indicators.note: plays about with, so the letters of Sport duke are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocratic sportsman plays a game that has countless versions.
explanation.definitionFit: This card game has numerous versions, such as five-card and seven-card forms.

clue.text: Old monarch, her hat edged with swirls

indicators.note: whirls about, so the letters of her hat edged with are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former king's lady wears a hat trimmed with swirling patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This British king abdicated in 1936 to marry Wallis Simpson.

clue.text: Provided with everything necessary, European told jokes

parts.note: quipped means made witty remarks

explanation.surface: A European fully kitted out cracks jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fitted out or furnished means having all that is needed.

clue.text: Element that's essential in alchemy?

parts.note: the letter at the very centre of alchemy is H, the chemical symbol of this gas; the surface suggests something vital to the alchemist's art

explanation.surface: Asks which element an alchemist could not do without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' means central: the middle letter of alchemy is H, symbol of the lightest element.
explanation.definitionFit: The lightest chemical element has the symbol H, which sits at the core of the word.

clue.text: Returning extremely defective rug, Greek character is wild

indicators.note: going back, so the assembled letters are read in reverse
only the extreme letters, first and last, of defective

parts.note: a mat is a small rug
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone sending back a faulty rug, with a Greek fellow involved, gets furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' runs the whole string backwards, so the Greek letter, last in the clue, ends up first; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Not domesticated or tamed means wild.

clue.text: One old man becoming enthralled by brown snake

indicators.note: captivated or held by, so these letters go inside the word for brown

parts.note: tan is a light brown
I is the Roman numeral one
pa is informal for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman finds himself captivated by a brown snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly venomous Australian snake goes by this name.

clue.text: Check car temperature

parts.note: Audi is a German car make
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: A mechanic checking a car's temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of accounts is a formal check.

clue.text: Distressing time — telephone about closure of factory

indicators.note: the phone call letters go around the closing letter

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word factory

explanation.surface: An upsetting moment: a phone call about a factory shutting down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closure' looks like a shutdown but is just the final letter, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to endure is upsetting or distressing.

clue.text: Shock as bottom falls out of hamper

indicators.note: in a down light the bottom is the last letter, which is dropped from the word for hamper

parts.note: to stunt growth is to hamper it

explanation.surface: A shocking moment when a picnic hamper's base gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket but is the verb, stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze or astonish someone is to shock them.

clue.text: On air, force to get reward

indicators.note: broadcast, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to prise is to force open with a lever

explanation.surface: A broadcast in which someone is forced to accept an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Something won for success or merit is a reward.

clue.text: Periods in history are brought up by son

indicators.note: in a down light, raised upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Historical periods are what a son was raised on.
explanation.definitionFit: Long distinct spans of history are called by this word for ages.

clue.text: Oscar and Dorothy struggling to embrace unknown doctrine

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: hug, so the jumbled letters wrap round the unknown
floundering, so the letters of Dorothy are rearranged

parts.note: x is the mathematician's unknown

explanation.surface: Two people, Oscar and Dorothy, wrestle with an obscure doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' turns DOROTHY into RTHODOY, which holds X; O goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepted, established belief or teaching is a body of doctrine.

clue.text: Some disquiet an American's shown about issue

indicators.note: turned round, so the run of letters is read backwards
only part of the words disquiet an American's is taken

explanation.surface: An American voices some unease about a contentious issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To flow out or proceed from a source is to issue from it.

clue.text: Cloth from Grandma having a fine edge

parts.note: nan is an informal name for a grandmother
a keen blade has a sharp, fine edge

explanation.surface: A grandmother's fabric with a delicate hem.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish cotton fabric originally from Nanjing is a kind of cloth.
